title: Why changing one object changes another
subtitle: References explain surprising mutation bugs
learning_objective: Predict how object references behave when assigned to another variable.

scenes.title: TWO VARIABLES, ONE OBJECT
scenes.body: You copy a variable, edit the copy, and suddenly the original data changes too.

scenes.title: Objects are referenced
scenes.body: Assigning an object to another variable copies the reference, not a second independent object. Both variables can point to the same object.

scenes.title: The surprise
Safer update
scenes.body: For a shallow copy of a simple object, use { ...a }. Nested objects are still shared unless you copy them too.

scenes.question: After `const b = a`, where do a and b point?
scenes.explanation: Assignment copies the reference. Mutating the shared object is visible through either variable.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Ask whether you copied the data or only copied a reference to it.
